default.p.tanki2_n4-t11-p1.vietnamese:
Do you like “travel (※1)”? When we travel, we can visit many different places, see new things, and enjoy delicious food. In addition, visiting a place for the first time gives us a fresh feeling. Since there are many means of transportation, we can easily travel to distant places.

For this reason, many people today probably think that “traveling is ① enjoyable.” ② However, in the past, there were no trains or cars, so ordinary people had to walk when traveling long distances. Dangerous things sometimes happened along the way, and people sometimes fell ill. In the past, a journey was not enjoyable; it was ③ harsh.

In classical Japanese literature, scenes often appear in which people setting out on long journeys and those seeing them off say goodbye while crying. This was probably because when people left on long journeys, they did not know whether they would return alive.

(※1) 旅 (journey): 旅行 (travel)

default.p.tanki2_n4-t8-p1.vietnamese:
The Small Shop Near My Home

Jeff

My favorite pen stopped writing. So I went out to buy a pen.

Normally, I would go to a large supermarket about a 15-minute walk from my home, but this time I tried a small shop nearby. I thought it might not have the pen I wanted, but it actually had exactly one. However, the pen was a little dirty.

An elderly woman was working alone in the shop. I said to her, “Please sell me this one,” and handed her the pen. Immediately, she asked, “This one is a little dirty, isn’t it? Is it still all right with you?” When I replied, “Yes, that’s fine,” she wiped the pen clean for me.

As I paid, I felt extremely happy and comfortable.

default.q.tanki2_n4-t10-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 黒坂駅から１２時５０分のバスに乗って行く。
Since Tanaka will be out in the morning and will not return to the company, he needs to go from Kurosaka Station instead. The 12:50 bus takes 10 minutes and arrives before the 1:30 p.m. deadline.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t10-q1.explanation: The pattern 「〜までに」 means “by〜” or “no later than〜” and states a deadline; here, the venue must be reached by 1:30. The relevant meaning is: “People who cannot go in the morning should arrive at the venue by 1:30 p.m.” The original passage states: 「午前中に行けない人は、午後１時半までに会場に行ってください。」 and 「黒坂駅からもバスがあります。駅から会場までは１０分ですが、１２時５０分発のバスのあとは１時３５分発なので、気をつけてください。」 To distinguish the tricky choices, remember that the 12:50 bus arrives within 10 minutes, while the 1:35 bus leaves after the 1:30 deadline.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 楽しい
The passage explains that traveling today allows people to visit various places, see unusual things, and eat delicious food. Therefore, many people think that “traveling is enjoyable.”
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q1.explanation: The pattern 「AはBものだ」expresses a general view or characteristic of A; here, 「旅は楽しいものだ」means “traveling is something enjoyable.” The sentence means: “Thus, nowadays, many people probably think that traveling is enjoyable.” The exact supporting sentence is: 「このように、今は『旅は楽しいものだ』と思う人が多いでしょう。」 The easiest option to confuse it with is 「悲しい」, but the passage shows enjoyment through seeing unusual things, eating delicious food, and gaining a new feeling; hardship belongs to travel in the past.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) しかし
「しかし」 expresses contrast. The previous sentence says that traveling is convenient and enjoyable today, while the following sentence describes how people had to walk and face dangers in the past.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q2.explanation: 「しかし」 means “however” and is used at the beginning of a sentence to connect two opposing ideas. The sentence means: “However, in the past, because there were no trains or cars, ordinary people had to travel on foot.” The exact supporting sentence is: 「しかし、むかしは、電車や車がなかったので、普通の人は歩いて旅をしなくてはなりませんでした。」 To distinguish it from 「そして」, remember that 「しかし」 signals the contrast between convenient travel today and difficult travel in the past, while 「そして」 merely joins ideas moving in the same direction.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 死ぬかもしれない
In the passage, travel in the past was very difficult because travelers could face danger or become ill. Therefore, 厳しい here implies that they might die during the journey.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q3.explanation: 厳しい means “harsh,” “severe,” or “difficult”; in this sentence, it describes journeys in the past as dangerous and physically demanding. The sentence means: “In the past, travel was not something enjoyable but something harsh and difficult.” The relevant original sentence is 「むかしは、旅は楽しいものではなく、厳しいものだったのです。」, followed by 「これは、旅に出ると、生きて帰ってくることができるかどうか、わからなかったからでしょう。」 To distinguish it from (c), remember that とても嫌だ means “to dislike something very much,” while 厳しい here refers to the danger and possibility of not returning alive, matching (a).
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 今は、旅は楽しいが、むかしはそうではなかった
The passage says that traveling is enjoyable and convenient today because people can visit places, eat delicious food, and travel far easily. In contrast, traveling in the past was difficult and dangerous, so it was not enjoyable.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t11-q4.explanation: The pattern 「Aが、B」 connects two contrasting ideas, while 「そうではなかった」 means “was not so”; therefore, choice b contrasts enjoyable travel today with harsh travel in the past. The sentence means: “Travel is enjoyable today, but it was not so in the past.” The direct evidence is: 「むかしは、旅は楽しいものではなく、③<u>厳しい</u>ものだったのです。」, while the passage also says that people can travel far easily today because of various means of transportation. Distinguish b from a and c: those choices incorrectly claim that travel was also enjoyable or equally difficult in the past.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t12-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 21日にB病院
A 25-year-old belongs to the ～34歳までの方 group, and the “women’s diseases” examination is available only on the second date, October 21, at B病院.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t12-q1.explanation: The pattern ～34歳までの方 means “people aged 34 or younger,” while ～にだけ means “only on ～” and limits when something is available. Since the woman is 25 and wants the 「女性の病気」 examination, she must choose date ② for her age group. Translation of the evidence: “People aged 34 or younger: ① October 7, ② October 21”; “① is held at A病院, and ② is held at B病院”; “The ‘women’s diseases’ examination is held only on date ②.” To avoid confusion, remember that October 7 is date ① at A病院, whereas October 21 is date ② at B病院; the weekend dates follow a separate special schedule.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t12-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 12日
October 12 is the second Saturday, when morning examinations are available, and it is before the business trip from October 15 to 22. Since he cannot take time off during weekday daytime, he must choose a weekend date.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t12-q2.explanation: The key reading point is that he must choose a weekend date because he cannot take time off during weekday daytime, while also avoiding his business trip. The relevant sentence means: “In October, reception is available only in the morning on the second Saturday and the third Sunday.” The exact basis in the passage is: 「10月は、第2土曜と第3日曜に、午前中のみ、受け付けます。」 and 「土曜日はA病院、日曜日はB病院で行います。」 To distinguish it from 20日, remember that both 12日 and 20日 are eligible weekend dates, but 20日 falls within his business trip.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) それで
「それで」 expresses a result or consequence. Because Jeff’s favorite pen stopped writing, he went out to buy a pen.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q1.explanation: 「それで」 connects a preceding reason or situation to a following result or action, meaning “so” or “therefore.” The sentence means: “My favorite pen stopped writing. So, I went out to buy a pen.” The exact supporting sentence is: 「好きなペンが書けなくなった。それで、ペンを買いに出かけた。」 A useful distinction is that 「すると」 mainly shows sequence—“then” or “when that happened”—whereas 「それで」 emphasizes the cause-and-effect relationship shown here.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) いつも
The expression いつもなら means “normally” or “if it is the usual case.” Here, Jeff explains that he would normally go to a large supermarket about 15 minutes from his house.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q2.explanation: The pattern いつもなら means “normally” or “if it is the usual case,” with いつも modifying なら. The sentence means: “Normally, I would go to a large supermarket about 15 minutes away on foot from my house.” The original sentence is: 「いつもなら家から歩いて15分ぐらいの大きいスーパーに行くのだが、近所にある小さい店に行ってみた。」To avoid confusion, remember the fixed pattern いつもなら, not いつもに, いつもと, or いつもだなら.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) ないかもしれない
「もしかしたら」expresses possibility, so the writer thought the pen he wanted might not be available. However, the shop actually had one pen.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q3.explanation: The pattern 「～かもしれない」means “might～” and expresses uncertainty; 「ないかもしれない」means “might not～.” The sentence means: “I thought the pen I wanted might not be available, but there was one.” The original sentence is: 「もしかしたら、わたしのほしいペンはないかもしれないと思ったが、1本だけあった。」To distinguish it from 「あるかもしれない」, notice that 「が」signals a contrast, so the first clause should express “might not be there” to contrast with the fact that one pen was actually found.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) では
In this sentence, 店では presents “at the shop” as the topic or emphasizes the setting. Therefore, the sentence says that an old woman was working alone at the shop.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q4.explanation: The pattern 店では consists of the place noun 店 plus では, meaning “at the shop,” with は presenting the place as the topic or giving it emphasis. The sentence means: “At the shop, an old woman was working alone.” The original sentence is: 「店ではおばあさんが一人ではたらいていた。」 The closest confusing option is 店で, because で also marks the place where an action occurs, but では additionally emphasizes or presents the shop as the topic or setting.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q5.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) と言って
In this sentence, Jeff says 「これをください。」 to the old woman and then hands over the pen, so と言って correctly connects the quoted speech with the following action.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t8-q5.explanation: The pattern 「N／quoted clause」と言う means “to say N／to say that…,” with と marking the content of what is said; と言って is the て-form used to connect it to the next action. The sentence means: “Saying to the old woman, ‘Please give me this,’ I handed over the pen.” The original sentence is: 店のおばあさんに「これをください。」と言って、ペンをわたした。A useful distinction is that と言う is used for making a statement or request, while と答える is used for answering a question; here, 「これをください。」 is not an answer.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t9-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 1日でいろいろなスポーツをするコースがあること
The passage clearly says that the club offers a course where learners can experience many sports in one day.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t9-q1.explanation: The pattern ～ために means “for” or “in order to,” while ～も用意しました means “also prepared,” adding another convenient option for people who do not know what the club is like. The relevant sentence means: “For people who do not know what kind of place it is, we have also prepared a course where they can experience many sports in one day.” The original sentence is: 「どんなところか わからない人のために、1日でたくさんのスポーツができるコースも用意しました。」 Distinguish this from (a): “10月から” only indicates when people want to start exercising, not that the new course begins in October.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) さとうさんはとても（しんせつ）なひとです。
The kanji「親切」is correctly read「しんせつ」in hiragana and means kind or considerate.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q1.explanation: The key word in the sentence is the na-adjective「親切（しんせつ）」, used to describe a kind, considerate personality or a warm, attentive attitude toward others. When modifying a noun, it takes「な」as in「親切な + noun」(e.g.,「親切な人」); when modifying a verb, it becomes「親切に + verb」(e.g.,「親切に教える」). The complete sentence means: "Mr./Ms. Sato is a very kind person." Another example is:「駅員さんが親切に道を教えてくれました。」(The station attendant kindly showed me the way.) When learning the kanji「親切」, note that both「親」(しん) and「切」(せつ) use short sounds; do not mistakenly add long vowels to produce しんせい or しんせつう.

The kanji 「特別」 has the correct hiragana reading 「とくべつ」 and expresses a degree that is notably different from and greater than normal.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q2.explanation: 「特別」(とくべつ) can function as a na-adjective before a noun, as in 特別な + N, and can also function as an adverb before an adjective or verb, in the form 特別 or 特別に, to emphasize something exceptional or different from usual. The complete sentence means: “It has been hot and humid every day recently, but today is especially hot.” To avoid kanji-reading confusion, remember the on-readings「とく」for「特」and「べつ」for「別」; do not replace them with an incorrect long vowel such as とう. Another example is:「きょうは特別に宿題が多いです。」(There is an especially large amount of homework today.)

default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q4.explanation: The Group 1 verb 「通る」（とおる）changes to 「通って」（とおって）in the て-form. It commonly combines with を in the pattern 「[place] を 通る/通って」to express moving through or passing across a specific space. The complete sentence means: “I often pass through this park on my way home.” A similar example is 「毎朝、この商店街を通って駅へ行きます。」(Every morning, I go to the station through this shopping district.) In the test, remember that moving through a place takes 「を」, not 「で」. Also, 通 has the long vowel とお, so do not confuse the pronunciation with とって or とうって.

The kanji 「中止」consists of 中 and 止. Its correct hiragana reading is 「ちゅうし」, meaning to cancel an event.
default.q.tanki2_n4-t1-q8.explanation: The key vocabulary 「中止」（ちゅうし）is a noun or noun-verb used with 「する」to mean canceling or suspending an event or planned activity because of bad weather or an unexpected problem. Combined with the conditional 「〜たら」, the complete sentence means: "If it rains, the concert will be canceled."
